newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU queries France on Air Liberte planned sale.
newsitem.headline: EU queries France on Air Liberte planned sale.

text.p: The European Commission is writing to France about the sale of insolvent Air Liberte following British Airways allegations that the deal may be in breach of EU fair competition rules, an EU source said on Monday.

British Airways Plc asked the Commission at the end of last week to block the reported acquisition of Air Liberte by French regional airline AOM, a subsidiary of state-owned Credit Lyonnais which is only surviving thanks to huge and repeated state bail outs.

In a letter to European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert and his transport counterpart Neil Kinnock, BA's chairman Robert Ayling said the AOM acquisition, if allowed, would be contrary to the Commission's July 1995 decision on Credit Lyonnais.
The letter calls "for immediate measures to block the bid", a Commission source said on Monday.
As a result, Van Miert's services were to send a letter to the French government as soon as Monday, asking it to clarify the conditions at which AOM would take over Air Liberte.

The Commission agreed in 1995 to a 45-billion French franc ($8.7 billion) restructuring plan for Credit Lyonnais involving the transfer of the bank's ailing assets, including AOM, to a state-backed structure for future privatisation.
The Commission's letter to the French government seeks to assess whether there is any state money involved in the acquisition of Air Liberte by AOM, the source said.

According to an article in French daily newspaper Le Monde the French government wants to put up a new airline by bringing together privately owned Eurolair, AOM and Air Liberte in order to keep out BA.
AOM denied on Friday that the company was part of a plan to buy Air Liberte to form a new group to keep British Airways at bay. But a AOM spokeswoman did not deny AOM was interested in the airline.

BA has said it would consider buying either AOM or Air Liberte to increase the number of landing and taking off slots at the Paris Orly airport. BA's French subsidiary TAT currently has only 21 slots at the capital's most-covered airport. Air Liberte has 37.
Air Liberte was placed under legal administration insolvency on September 26.

The Commission is currently waiting for the France to submit fresh proposals to get Lyonnais back on its feet as it became clear that the 1995 rescue plan, the second in two years, failed to reach that purpose. -- Amelia Torres 322 2876841 ($ = 5.174 French Francs)
